sources.name: Tom's Hardware GPU 계층표 2026 (1080p Ultra)
sources.note: Current raster table, 1080p Ultra column (fps = geomean of 11 games), Ryzen 7 9800X3D testbed; article updateDate 2026-06-24. Ray-tracing table ignored. No GTX 1060 here, so it is bridged to the 2022-2024 table (tomsSuiteBridge).

sources.name: Tom's Hardware GPU 계층표 2022–2024 (1080p Ultra)
sources.note: First table on page 2 (raster, 8 games, Core i9-12900K), 1080p Ultra column. GTX 1060 6GB = 32.1 fps defines 100. No longer updated. Second table on that page is ray tracing (ignored). Cards above ~105 fps are CPU-limited at 1080p.

sources.name: Tom's Hardware GPU 계층표 2020–2021
sources.note: Score % = geomean of 9 games x 6 resolution/setting combos (not 1080p Ultra alone), Core i9-9900K. Used only for Intel UHD Graphics 630, normalized to its own GTX 1060 6GB (26.5%). The 4388-4 URL redirected to page 1 (no separate table found).

sources.name: PassMark G3D Mark
sources.note: Synthetic G3D Mark. 'GeForce GTX 1060' = 10017 (3GB has its own entry, so treated as 6GB). Used only where Tom's has no data.

tomsSuiteBridge.method: rel = T1_fps x F / 32.1 x 100, where F = median(T2_fps / T1_fps) over models in both the 2026 and 2022-2024 Tom's tables with T2 1080p Ultra <= 105 fps (GPU-bound region; RX 7600 XT excluded as anomalous). For 2022-24-only cards above 105 fps (RTX 3080 12GB, RX 6800, RX 7900 GRE) the T2 value is divided by the median T2/T1 ratio of the 4 nearest overlap models (by T2 fps) and then multiplied by F, to undo CPU compression.
tomsSuiteBridge.note: Above ~105 fps the T2/T1 ratio falls steadily to 0.84 (RTX 4090), showing 12900K CPU limits in the older table.

bridge.method: PassMark relative = G3D / G3D('GeForce GTX 1060') x 100, then multiplied by factor. factor = median over overlap models of (Tom's 2022-24 1080p Ultra relative / PassMark relative). spreadPct = population std-dev of the ratios / median x 100.
